answer: Rotating audit juries stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each new agent gets five peers chosen at random. Second, the jury samples its jobs and signs a verdict, so fakes cannot pick friendly judges. Third, jurors are paid only when later audits confirm their verdict, punishing lazy approval. Fourth, a guilty verdict freezes earnings ninety days and bars re-entry for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 5,000 approvals, about $15,000 in fees, and 10,000 real jobs. Trust winds like a spiral thread through honest timber work, like stallholders inspecting each other before earning a pitch.
